subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

By the skin of your teeth

options.text: To be less affected by criticisms and rebuffs

solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"By the skin of your teeth"** means something that is achieved or escaped by a very narrow margin. (बहुत ही कम अंतर से हासिल करना या बचना)

 
 
• **Example: **He caught the last train **by the skin of his teeth.**
 
 
 
• **"By a very narrow margin"** refers to something that is just barely accomplished or avoided. (बहुत कम अंतर से)
 
 
• **Example: **She passed the exam **by a very narrow margin.**
 
 

Therefore, the correct meaning of the given idiom is **'By a very narrow margin.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: To be less affected by criticisms and rebuffs** (आलोचनाओं और अस्वीकृतियों से कम प्रभावित होना)

 
 
• **Example:** She has developed a thick skin over the years and is** less affected by criticisms and rebuffs.**
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Very protective** (बहुत सुरक्षात्मक)
 
 
• **Example: **He is **very protective** of his younger sister.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Saved by others** (दूसरों द्वारा बचाया गया)
 
 
• **Example:** He was **saved by others **when he got into trouble.
 
 

210:Tdb6,

The correct answer is **Option 3)**
